claim: Moselsteig Stage 8 (Leiwen – Neumagen-Dhron) is a vineyard-and-rock-cliff stage ending in Germany's oldest wine town at the Stella Noviomagi Roman ship replica.
quote: On this unique stage between Leiwen and Neumagen-Dhron you walk through idyllic vineyards and past wild rock cliffs. The path ends in Neumagen-Dhron, the oldest wine town in Germany, at the dock of the 'Stella Noviomagi'

claim: Moselsteig Stage 8 Leiwen–Neumagen-Dhron is 14.09 km; Stage 9 Neumagen-Dhron–Kesten 17.97 km; Stage 10 Kesten–Bernkastel-Kues 14.69 km; Stage 11 Bernkastel-Kues–Ürzig 16.99 km; Stage 7 Mehring–Leiwen 14.50 km; Stage 6 Schweich–Mehring 12.38 km.
quote: 5 Trier – Schweich 19.91 km | 6 Schweich – Mehring 12.38 km | 7 Mehring – Leiwen 14.50 km | 8 Leiwen – Neumagen-Dhron 14.09 km | 9 Neumagen-Dhron – Kesten/Osann-Monzel 17.97 km | 10 Kesten/Osann-Monzel – Bernkastel-Kues 14.69 km | 11 Bernkastel-Kues – Ürzig 16.99 km

claim: Moselsteig Stage 11 (Bernkastel-Kues – Ürzig) is roughly 16.7 km with ~684 m elevation gain, rated difficult and takes 5.5-6 hours.
quote: The trail is 16.7 km long... elevation gain is 684 m... considered a difficult/hard hike... takes an average of 5.5–6 hours

claim: The Calmont Klettersteig between Bremm and Ediger-Eller is 3.54 km, ~1.5 h, +186 m / -210 m, medium difficulty, traversing Europe's steepest vineyard with ladders, steel cables and rock-ridge sections — but it lies ~40-50 km drive from Piesport (28.7 km straight line), at the outer edge of a day-trip radius.
quote: Distance: 3.54 km - Duration: Approximately 1.5 hours - Elevation gain: 186 m - Elevation loss: 210 m - Difficulty: Medium... constructed in 2002... steel cables, ladders, as well as numerous steps and pegs

claim: The Calmont rises 380 m between Bremm and Ediger-Eller with up to 65° incline (Europe's steepest vineyard) and is secured with 6 ladders, ~100 m of safety rope, 22 step irons and 16 grip pegs; sure-footedness and freedom from dizziness required but no via-ferrata kit needed.
quote: Between Bremm and Ediger-Eller it rises 380 meters high... an incline of up to 65 degrees, it is Europe's steepest vineyard... 6 ladders are installed, approximately 100 meters of safety ropes, 22 step irons and 16 grip pegs

claim: The Piesporter Moselbogen 'Leuchtpunkt' circular hike is 7.98 km, ~2 h 15 min, easy, with 105 m ascent / 205 m descent, running through the Goldtröpfchen vineyard past the St. Michael church and a Roman wine press, starting at the Bürgerhaus Piesport.
quote: approximately 7.98 kilometers and takes around 2 hours and 15 minutes... Rated as easy... 105 meters of ascent and 205 meters of descent... distinctive amphitheater-like Mosel bend

claim: The Zummethöhe panorama between Leiwen and Trittenheim was voted 'Best of the Vineyard Views – Moselle' in 2016 and is reached from a car park where the Kronenberg and Sonnenberg circular trails join to form a 15 km loop.
quote: voted 'Best of the Vineyard Views - Moselle' in 2016... Kronenberg circular (downstream direction) and Sonnenberg circular (upstream direction) meet at the Zummethöhe car park to form a 15 km-long trail

claim: The Fünf-Seen-Blick is a freely accessible 23 m wooden tower in the forest between Detzem and Mehring, with 105 steps to the top platform giving views from Schweich to Klüsserath and into the Eifel; it sits directly on Moselsteig Stage 7.
quote: 23 meter high wooden tower located about 25 kilometers from Trier... Climbing the 105 steps to the upper platform... grand view over the Moselle valley from Schweich to Klüsserath and far into the Eifel... directly on the Stefan-Andres hiking trail and on Moselsteig trail stage 07

claim: The Seitensprung Mehringer Schweiz partner-trail loop covers ~13.7 km with ~575 m of climbing, takes 4.5-5 hours, and includes the Fünf-Seen-Blick tower plus the Triolago recreation lake and Roman Villa Mehring.
quote: covers 8.5 miles (approximately 13.7 km), with an elevation gain of 1,886 feet (approximately 575 meters) and takes about 4.5–5 hours... 20-metre high wooden viewing tower... 'Five Moselle lakes'

claim: The Römersteig premium trail runs 22.26 km one-way from Hinkelstein near Trittenheim to Minheim, with +435 m / -300 m, rated difficult, crossing the Mosel twice and passing slate caves, Roman archaeological sites and a reconstructed wine press at Piesport.
quote: spans '22,26 km' and takes approximately '6 hours 20 minutes'... features '435 m' of ascent and '300 m' of descent... Rated as 'difficult'... begins 'at Hinkelstein bei 54349 Trittenheim' and concludes 'in 54518 Minheim'

claim: Moselsteig Stage 7 (Mehring – Leiwen) climbs through fir/spruce forest and beech high-forest in the Mehringer Schweiz and features a 20 m wooden viewing tower over the 'Five Moselle lakes' bends.
quote: challenging stage leads through the woodland around Mehringer Schweiz... steep paths through fir and spruce forests, through a high-level beech forest... 20-metre high wooden viewing tower... 'Five Moselle lakes'

claim: The Panorama-Wanderweg Piesport is a ~5 km loop starting and ending at the Piesporter Heiligenhäuschen car park, leading to the Weislei shelter and the 'Großer Moselblick' viewpoint that gives a 180° panorama over Piesport, Minheim and Neumagen-Dhron.
quote: approximately 5 kilometers long... 180 degree panorama over the Moselle valley with the wine villages of Piesport, Minheim and Neumagen-Dhron... begins and ends at the 'Piesporter Heiligenhäuschen' car park

claim: Moselsteig Stage 7 from Mehring to Leiwen is a partner-stage of the Seitensprung Mehringer Schweiz and is considered one of the more demanding stages of the Moselsteig.
The Saar-Hunsrück region holds 112 Traumschleifen (premium circular loops) of 6-20 km and 24 shorter Traumschleifchen up to 7 km, certified by the German Hiking Institute and themed individually.
quote: 112 Traumschleifen (dream loops) and 24 Traumschleifchen... between 6 and 20 km long, designed as circular routes... designed according to German Hiking Institute standards

claim: The Moselachter premium loop at Trittenheim is ~14 km (8.8 mi) with ~412 m (1,351 ft) climbing, rated moderate, 4-4.5 hours, with views into both the Mosel and Dhron valleys.
quote: Moselachter is a trail located in Trittenheim... covers 8.8 mi, with an elevation gain of 1,351 ft and takes about 4–4.5 hr to complete

claim: The Piesporter Goldtröpfchen vineyard slopes range from 30% to 70% gradient and recommended footwear is hiking/trekking shoes with provisions.
quote: vineyards have slopes ranging from 30 to 70 percent, with some being extremely steep... hiking or trekking shoes are recommended, as well as provisions in a backpack
